Welcome back to PharmacyInsider.

If you have followed my previous posts 

you already know Magnesium Glycinate is 

best for sleep and anxiety, and 

Magnesium Citrate is best for 

constipation relief.

Today let me introduce you to a third 

type — one of the most commonly sold 

forms in our pharmacy because it is 

inexpensive and works for two very 

common problems.

Magnesium Oxide.

---

What Is Magnesium Oxide?

Magnesium Oxide is magnesium combined 

with oxygen. It contains the highest 

percentage of elemental magnesium 

compared to other forms — but here is 

the catch — your body absorbs it the 

least efficiently of all magnesium 

types.

This sounds like a disadvantage but it 

is actually exactly why this form 

works so well for two specific 

purposes.

---

How Magnesium Oxide Actually Works

Because your body absorbs Magnesium 

Oxide poorly, most of it stays in 

your digestive system rather than 

entering your bloodstream. This 

creates two useful effects:

1. Acid Neutralization

Magnesium Oxide directly neutralizes 

stomach acid. This is why it is 

commonly found in heartburn and 

antacid products. If you experience 

acidity or heartburn after meals, 

this form provides fast relief.

2. Stool Softening

The unabsorbed magnesium draws water 

into your intestines, softening stool 

and stimulating bowel movement. This 

makes it effective for constipation 

relief — similar to Magnesium Citrate 

but generally gentler and slower 

acting.

---

What Customers Use It For Most

From my pharmacy experience these 

are the top reasons customers buy 

Magnesium Oxide:

✓ Heartburn and acid reflux

✓ Occasional constipation

✓ General magnesium supplementation 

  when budget is a concern

✓ Indigestion after heavy meals

---

Important — Side Effects to Know

Magnesium Oxide is generally safe but 

because of how it works in your 

digestive system, side effects are 

common at higher doses:

⚠️ Diarrhea — the most common side 

 effect, especially at higher doses

⚠️ Stomach pain or cramping

⚠️ Nausea

These side effects usually mean the 

dose is too high for your body. 

Reducing the amount typically resolves 

this quickly.

---

Pharmacy Counseling Points

When I counsel customers on Magnesium 

Oxide I always cover these three things:

1. Always take with water

A full glass of water helps the 

supplement work properly and reduces 

stomach irritation.

2. Never exceed the recommended dose

More is not better with this 

supplement. Taking extra will not 

provide additional benefit — it will 

simply increase your risk of diarrhea 

and stomach discomfort.

3. Kidney patients must consult a 

 doctor first

This is critical. People with kidney 

disease cannot effectively remove 

excess magnesium from their body. 

For these patients, taking Magnesium 

Oxide without medical supervision can 

lead to dangerously high magnesium 

levels — a condition called 

Hypermagnesemia.

---

Magnesium Oxide vs Other Forms — 

Quick Comparison

MAGNESIUM OXIDE:

→ Best for heartburn and acidity

→ Also helps constipation

→ Cheapest option

→ Lowest absorption rate

→ More likely to cause diarrhea

MAGNESIUM CITRATE:

→ Best specifically for constipation

→ Faster acting than oxide

→ Better absorbed than oxide

MAGNESIUM GLYCINATE:

→ Best for sleep and anxiety

→ Highest absorption rate

→ Gentlest on the stomach

→ Safe for daily long term use
